summary: Build water tariff models, cost-of-service analysis, subsidy designs, and regulatory submissions. Enrol in this practical five-day course.
lede: Water tariff design training helps finance managers, analysts and regulators link charges to service costs and customer affordability. Participants build revenue-requirement models, allocate costs by customer class, compare fixed and volumetric charges, test bill impacts and targeted subsidies, and prepare supporting evidence for tariff submissions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who prepare, review, regulate, finance, or communicate water utility tariffs and revenue plans. It suits mixed institutional cohorts where finance, commercial, public-sector, regulatory, and development perspectives must work from a shared evidence base.
modules: Water Tariff Economics and Service Context
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to water utility finance, tariff review, regulatory analysis, public finance, or utility commercial operations. Basic spreadsheet literacy is required, but coding is not. Advanced tariff economics and digital analytics are taught at operational application level, while AI-assisted analysis is introduced as a supervised review technique rather than production implementation. Bring a laptop with spreadsheet software; no programming environment is required.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
